definitions.explanation: A shop specializing in selling hats, or a person who makes or sells hats.

examples.japanese: {駅前|えきまえ}に{帽子屋|ぼうしや}がある。
examples.english: There's a hat shop in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {帽子屋|ぼうしや}で{夏用|なつよう}の{麦|むぎ}わら{帽子|ぼうし}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought a straw hat for summer at a hat shop.

examples.japanese: この{商店街|しょうてんがい}に{昔|むかし}からある{帽子屋|ぼうしや}は、{手作|てづく}りの{帽子|ぼうし}で{知|し}られている。
examples.english: The hat shop that has been in this shopping street for a long time is known for its handmade hats.

notes:
A compound of {帽子|ぼうし} (hat) and {屋|や} (shop, dealer). The suffix {屋|や} is one of the most productive word-forming elements in Japanese, attaching to products to create shop names: {花屋|はなや} (flower shop), {本屋|ほんや} (bookshop), {魚屋|さかなや} (fish shop), etc.

{帽子屋|ぼうしや} can also refer to the person who runs the shop (the hatter), following the same pattern as {八百屋|やおや} (greengrocer, or the greengrocery).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {帽子屋|ぼうしや}で{買|か}う: to buy at a hat shop
- {帽子屋|ぼうしや}の{店主|てんしゅ}: the owner of a hat shop
- {老舗|しにせ}の{帽子屋|ぼうしや}: a long-established hat shop

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {帽子|ぼうし}{専門店|せんもんてん}: hat specialty store — more modern and formal expression
- {洋品店|ようひんてん}: Western clothing store — a broader category that may include hats
- {靴屋|くつや}: shoe shop — follows the same {product}+{屋|や} pattern
